This yields x=(a²+b²)/(a+b), x=0, or x=a+b. The condition |a|≠|b| ensures a+b≠0 and a≠b. The first root differs from a and b by b(b−a)/(a+b) and a(a−b)/(a+b), respectively, both nonzero. The other two roots also avoid a,b because ab≠0. Finally, the first root is nonzero and differs from a+b by −2ab/(a+b), so all three are distinct.
